rows.evidence: src/core/work-graph/state/run-machine.ts:1217 is the then-arm of locatorShapeOk; locatorAfter (:1229-1266) builds the new locator only from the caller's RunObservedHistory. The three entry writers supply it: recordExecutionEntered requires positive start/observed (src/core/work-graph/tasks/execution-entry-service.ts:1684 with observedHistoryProblem at :2060-2066); recordExecutionHistory requires the same (src/core/work-graph/tasks/execution-history-service.ts:147, :168); and recordRunResult's only callers take startPosition from a codec-validated persisted locator or from a Kernel turn.started position: src/core/agent-runtime/execution-observation.ts:522 (isRunExecutionHistoryV1), :742-747 (startPosition: locator.startPosition), :855; src/core/agent-runtime/run-reconcile.ts:346, :396 (locator?.startPosition ?? start.position), :621 (start.position, always >= afterPosition+1). No route, tool, runtime or recovery path passes a non-positive start. (recordRunResult itself does not re-check positions: execution-entry-service.ts:1775-1798.)
rows.proposal_note: Deleting the check is behaviour-preserving for today's only callers, and locatorShapeOk has no other call site (:1242, :1252), no switch/type dependency and no spec line asking the machine to re-derive the shape (RUN-06 row, docs/refactor/STATE-MACHINES-SPEC.md:1869). But recordRunResult has no positive-position input check of its own, so prefer claude's variant: either keep :1242 as the machine's input check, or add the positive-position check to recordRunResult (execution-entry-service.ts:1775-1798) before dropping the positivity line here; codex's bare deletion would leave that port unvalidated (no behaviour change today).

rows.evidence: run.executionHistory is only ever read from a decoded RunSnapshot. src/core/work-graph/materials/record-readers.ts:202-204 rejects any Run whose executionHistory fails isRunExecutionHistoryV1, and that validator is at least as strict as locatorShapeOk: it also requires the exact keys (src/core/work-graph/persistence/execution-history-codecs.ts:74, :78, :82) and positive start/observed, a null-or-positive end, start<=observed and end in [start,observed] (:91-94). The Run codec does not cross-check status/phase (:248 is status only), but the locator itself is fully checked, so even a hand-edited store row fails to decode before transitionRun and :1252's then-arm is unreachable; the before-T test at .dsh-ref/before/tests/state/run-machine.test.ts:852-855 bypassed the store by hand-building the RunSnapshot, and no after-T test does. The same predicate at :1242 guards every locator locatorAfter writes.
rows.proposal_note: Deleting the check at :1252 and its 'the stored executionHistory is malformed' failure changes no decodable record's behaviour; locatorShapeOk then has only the :1242 call site (or none, if A1-018 is removed too), nothing else calls it, no switch or type depends on the failure, and I found no spec line requiring the stored-locator refusal (RUN-06 only fixes identity/start, monotone watermark and write-once end, STATE-MACHINES-SPEC.md:1869).

rows.evidence: Only src/core/work-graph/state/run-machine.ts:876-877 writes phase 'entered', and it writes status 'running' in the same record (enteredRunRecord). reconciledEndRecord (:987-1003) writes 'settled'/'unknown' together with status 'ended' (:993). rows.evidence: src/core/work-graph/state/task-failure.ts:1109 returns early for chain 'none'; :1110-1116 then builds the facts, and the arm is head===null inside anchor===null. src/core/work-graph/tasks/plan-service.ts:916-919 makes head null exactly when chain.kind!=='head' and anchorRun null when head is null (or the anchored Run was not read), so this arm needs a chain that is not 'none' but has no head, i.e. roundChainHead 'invalid' (src/core/work-graph/state/verification-machine.ts:477-512: two roots, ordinal gap, foreign subject, non-finalized predecessor). Every platform writer keeps one root and linked successors: roundOnOpened claims the subject slot null->owner (:1549-1570), buildSuccessorRound writes ordinal+1/predecessor (:629-676), roundOnReverified moves the same slot (:1506-1535); the gate slot key excludes runId (:125-135), so no second root. The round codec checks only the per-record chain shape (src/core/work-graph/persistence/evidence-record-codecs.ts:231-260; cross-record linearity is explicitly left to roundChainHead at :234), so a hand-written row reaches it (the before-T test committed two chain-less roots with commitRaw, .dsh-ref/before/tests/work-graph/A2-gate-chain-facts.test.ts:218-245). No platform writer or public step produces an invalid chain.
rows.proposal_note: Keep the bad-chain diagnostic untested is right (rule 4; decision 79-4). Codex's extra 'delete the old-root compatibility input' has no target left here: roundOrdinalOf reads chain.ordinal directly (verification-machine.ts:98) and TP-025 already removed the default. Claude's optional GAP-52 note (give tests/state/task-failure.test.ts:1288 anchorRun:null) is a test-fixture choice that would exercise the arm but still not make the state reachable by public steps, so it does not change the class.

rows.evidence: src/core/work-graph/state/verification-machine.ts:821 is the `?? null` of step.check.incompleteCause for an interrupted check. The only writer of an interrupted check is changedCheck (:989-991), fed by CheckPhaseChange {phase:'interrupted'; incompleteCause: CheckInterruptionCause} (:935-936), and the only event that produces an interrupted check is check_interrupted with a required cause host_restart|ticket_invalid (:1639-1651); the replay event decoder is stricter still, requiring the check's incompleteCause to equal the event cause (persistence/evidence-record-codecs.ts:526-537). But the persisted-shape codec explicitly admits an interrupted check with the field absent or null ('C5: absent on legacy checks', evidence-record-codecs.ts:182-187; incompleteCauseProblem accepts null, persistence/rework-codecs.ts:228-231), so a legacy or hand-edited row reaches :821. No platform writer omits the cause.
rows.proposal_note: Deleting the arm and tightening the codec is safe for all current writers; the same change must update the contract type that still says 'absent on legacy checks' (src/contracts/verification.ts:148) and the spec lines that still say legacy absent reads as null (STATE-MACHINES-SPEC.md:2949, :3064, :3665), which TP-137 already orders. Then :821 can read the cause directly.
